title: Multi-SDK connection smoothing, stream ergonomics, and coordinated version bumps
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: Customers and internal e2e tests reported intermittent stream disconnects and token-refresh races during high churn workloads. Additionally, SDK ergonomics diverged across languages for backpressure hints and retry predicates. This PR implements a coordinated, minimal-surface set of changes across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs to reduce reconnect churn, provide a compact retry configuration, and align streaming ergonomics. Work completed (checklist): - [x] Introduce lightweight connection smoothing layer (dampening + jittered backoff) in all SDKs to avoid rapid reconnect storms. - [x] Add a small circuit-state cache so transient auth failures don't trigger immediate reconnect floods. - [x] Unify RetryPolicy names and docs (RetryPolicy -> RetryProfile) and provide backward-compatible alias shims. - [x] Python: add async generator backpressure hints and default retry presets (py SDK bumped to 1.12.0). - [x] TypeScript: introduce generator-based stream helper `createBufferedAsyncStream` and export compact retry builder (ts SDK bumped to 1.28.0). - [x] Go: add ConnPool.DelayedRetry fence and make pool dial jitter configurable (go SDK bumped to v1.5.3). - [x] Cross-SDK integration tests and flakiness mitigations added to CI. - [x] Docs updates: cross-language streaming migration guide and sample snippets. Implementation notes: - Connection smoothing is intentionally conservative: it adds a two-tier damping window (short-term 2–6s, long-term 20–40s) with randomized jitter per-client to avoid synchronized reconnect storms. It does not change application-visible APIs. - The RetryProfile is a small ergonomic wrapper that maps historical RetryPolicy options to a single compact builder; existing constructors map to the new shape via a thin alias layer to preserve compatibility. - Stream ergonomics changes focus on offering optional helpers rather than mandatory API surface changes. For Python we expose `with backpressure(hint_ms=100)` on async generators; for TypeScript we ship `createBufferedAsyncStream({maxBufferedMessages, hintMs})`; for Go we add a NewConnPool option `WithDialJitter(min,max)` and `WithRetryFence(duration)`. Backwards compatibility and rollout: - All shims are additive; there are no breaking signature changes. - We added deprecation warnings where names are aliased to the new API. - Minor docs callouts show migration snippets. CI and testing: - Added cross-sdk integration matrix job that exercises token refresh + reconnect under load and asserts no more than 3 reconnects/minute per logical client in steady-state. - Several flaky tests were stabilized by increasing time windows and mocking clock jitter in unit tests. Observability and telemetry: - New metrics: sdk.conn.smooth_backoff_applied (counter), sdk.conn.reconnect_spike (gauge), sdk.retry.profile_used (tagged). - Console docs mention how these metrics map to rollout heuristics. Related: SUP-984 incident postmortem and ENG-1423 follow-ups. Risks and mitigation: - Risk: long-lived clients may experience slightly longer recovery delays in edge cases; mitigation: damping windows are tunable via environment/config for enterprise installs. - Risk: subtle differences in RNG/jitter across runtimes; mitigation: we validated with targeted load tests and observed coherent behavior across languages. Links and references: - Migration guide: https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk/migrations/stream-ergonomics - Incident: https://linear.app/redwood/incident/SUP-984 - Tests: ci/infra/integration/multi-sdk-reconnect-matrix.yml

refactor(retry): introduce RetryProfile builder and add compatibility aliases

feat(ts): add createBufferedAsyncStream helper + export compact retry builder (1.28.0)

review_thread: Alex Kim: Can you call out why we need two damping windows (short + long) instead of a single exponential backoff?
Priya Nair: Short window handles transient network hiccups; long window prevents client thrash under repeated auth flaps. Added explanatory comments and tests.
Daniel Ruiz: Suggest exposing a single env var for enterprise installers to tune both windows together. Priya: added WITH_CONN_DAMPEN_FACTOR env and documented it in the installer notes.
Maya Chen: TS helper looks good; request to add a minimal example in README. Priya: added example and unit test.
Alex Kim: Found a race in Go ConnPool Close while reconnect is inflight. Priya: pushed a fix (pool:guardClose) and added a deterministic test to reproduce and validate fix.
Daniel Ruiz: CI flaky test resolved for python by mocking monotonic clock; approving after green CI.
Maya Chen: Approved. Alex Kim: Approved. Merge queued and squashed after CI rerun (one transient flaky lint fixed).
release_notes: Cross-SDK: introduce connection smoothing to reduce reconnect storms; unify retry surface to RetryProfile; ergonomic streaming helpers for Python/TypeScript/Go; minor version bumps: py 1.12.0, ts 1.28.0, go v1.5.3; new telemetry metrics for connection smoothing.
notes: Rollout plan: staged rollout for Hosted API customers, config toggles for Dedicated/Private installs
Follow-ups: ENG-1501 will evaluate exposing adaptive profiles at runtime and richer telemetry sampling
Backport candidates: internal support requested a hotfix for 1.11.x Python branch; created pr-271315-backport-1.11.x-conn-smoothing-py
